client_brief:
In Memory of Walter Fernwood: Service print run

Project overview
This is a family memorial keepsake for Walter Fernwood, who died at ninety four. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Service print run, keepsake cards plus the framed A4 memorial page, Memory book and keepsake share card as one editable document plus its source, and Fernwood plate set, twenty six scans across four eras plus one licensed cover frame.

What we will provide
shoebox_scans/ (26 files, mixed 1200 to 4800 px); keepsake_card_2019_press.pdf; framed_page_2019_press.pdf; guest_list.xlsx export; eulogy.txt and transcriptions.txt. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- Service print run, keepsake cards plus the framed A4 memorial page: One A6 keepsake card per household attending, in list order, each binding the name and the sister's relationship line in full at trim plus that family branch's plate, accompanied by the A4 framed memorial page rendered as a single record at true print...
- Memory book and keepsake share card as one editable document plus its source: One professionally selected Adobe Express template adapted to the supplied brand, copy, and approved imagery. 
- Fernwood plate set, twenty six scans across four eras plus one licensed cover frame: Every usable scan brought to one printable house look (one black point, one sense of warmth, one weight of print) with a deliberate era level decision recorded where a run could not be brought to the set, plus the postcard reverses raised to legibility...

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$6,000-$12,000 fixed; target delivery 4 to 6 weeks; direction approval, first-production proof, and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork family history restoration brief in which a private individual digitising roughly twenty four antique 1910 postcard photographs of a touring stage magician company asks for the photographic FRONT and the handwritten BACK of each, delivered legible for a printed memorial book and for sharing with family. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com posting from an individual with 'several old photo scans' to restore 'for A4 printing to mount on my wall', naming 'color fading', 'scratches or tears' and 'blurriness'. That second conceit is deliberately not taken at face value, because the three damages it names are precisely what this connector cannot do: there is no heal, clone or inpaint to rebuild a torn corner or a scratch crossing photographic texture, and no sharpen for blurriness. The honest fuller commission the same client actually needs is the one built here: the scans brought to one printable house look by tonal and colour means, damage handled by crop, plate scale and placement rather than faked, and the result carried into a keepsake the family can print and keep editing. No real person, family, troupe, venue or trademark is named; the magician company is the fictional Veranda Marvelli Company with a fictional lead Aldo Marvelli, and the Fernwood family, Walter Fernwood and the Allsop and Vance funeral home are invented for this benchmark. Verdict STRENGTHEN: the ledger concept was a restoration pass plus a book, which sat on one surface and promised repairs the tools cannot make.

price_band_and_audience: Heritage and memorial commission, 300 to 600 dollars, family and mourners aged 45 to 75, most of them reading printed pages rather than screens. The band is load-bearing in both directions. This is not a luxury commemorative volume, so gilt edges, foil rules, full bleed dramatic plates and a designer typographic conceit read as expensive theatre at a Congregational hall and against the mother's 2019 card on the same shelf. Nor is it a discount photo book, so a dense grid of small plates, drop shadows, decorative corners, script headings and a bright cheerful palette cheapen the keepsake and are exactly what the client says was done badly last time. What the money buys at this band is restraint: generous white space, a quiet classical text face at a size a seventy year old reads without glasses, plates given room, captions that are plain, and an unbroken calm from the contents page to the colophon. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the occasion even if every plate is technically clean. A real posting of this shape runs 350 to 900 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: A private heritage and memorial keepsake commissioned by a family for a service and to keep afterwards.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Commissioned 2024 by the Fernwood family, Brattleboro, Vermont, for a service of around sixty people at the Congregational hall.
brand_identity.about: This is a family memorial keepsake for Walter Fernwood, who died at ninety four. It is a book, not a photo album: plates with captions, a contents page, and the granddaughter's eulogy laid out in the middle, alongside a framed page and a small card for mourners to take home. The visual voice is set by two things: the family's wish that nothing be brightened or invented, and the funeral home pieces made for Walter's late wife in 2019, which the new work should sit beside on the shelf.
brand_identity.audience: The family and around sixty mourners aged 45 to 75, most of them reading printed pages rather than screens, many of whom remember the people in the photographs.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Heritage and memorial commission, 300 to 600 dollars. Neither a luxury commemorative volume with gilt and foil, nor a discount photo book with grids and script headings. What the money buys is restraint.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet classical text face set large enough for a seventy year old to read without glasses, paired with a modest sans for captions and contents. Generous white space, plates given room, plain captions, one unbroken calm from the contents page to the colophon. No script, no decorative corners.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, gentle, unsentimental. Lets the photographs and the family's own words carry. Example line the book would write: The company toured for eleven seasons, and this is his father's hand on the back of the card. No cheerfulness, no exclamation points.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no brand file. The look is inherited from the funeral home's two 2019 press files (a keepsake card and a framed page) that the family wants matched so the pieces sit together on the shelf, and from the family's own scans, eulogy and typed transcriptions. The funeral home's designer has retired and left only flat press files. Damage in the scans is to be shown honestly, handled by crop and placement rather than painted over.
brand_identity.values: Nothing invented and nothing brightened. Honesty to the photographs as they are, and a keepsake the family can keep editing until the day of the service.

assets_supplied.name: shoebox_scans/ (26 files, mixed 1200 to 4800 px)
assets_supplied.kind: Flatbed and phone scans spanning four eras: 1910 postcard photographs of a touring company with handwriting on the reverse, 1930s studio portraits on mount card, a 1968 colour run, 1990s drugstore prints and recent phone frames.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything my brother could scan. Some of them are damaged and we would rather see the damage than see it painted over."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the 1968 colour prints have shifted so far in their dye layers that no correction within reach brings them to the same neutral as the rest without taking the skin green, which is discoverable only by running the correction and looking at the result beside the others. Separately, four scans are photographs of framed prints rather than scans of prints, carrying glass reflection and keystone, and the postcard reverses are pencil on cream card sitting in so narrow a tonal band that the move which makes them legible also greys the card unless it is confined.

assets_supplied.name: keepsake_card_2019_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The funeral home's flat press file for the A6 keepsake card handed to mourners at the 2019 service, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout. Carries a name line, a relationship line, a date line and a placed photograph.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What they printed for my mother. We would like the same shape of thing so the two sit together on the shelf."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The relationship line sits in a fixed measure frame sized for the two and three word entries the 2019 list happened to hold. Longer entries do not spill and do not error, they simply stop rendering at the frame's last line, so a merged card looks finished and complete at thumbnail while a mourner's line is cut mid phrase at trim. The frame's true capacity depends on the applied face and size the retired designer set, which no readout states.

assets_supplied.name: framed_page_2019_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The funeral home's flat press file for the A4 framed memorial page from the 2019 service, with a large plate area, a name and dates, and a short verse block.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The page we framed for my mother. Same size, same place on the wall."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The plate area is a portrait proportion graphic frame while most of the scans worth framing are landscape, and how the merge fits or fills a placed image into that frame, whether it centres and what it clips, appears in no readout and is visible only on the rendered page. The page also carries no bleed and no bleed can be introduced, so any plan that runs a plate to the paper edge is unbuildable.

assets_supplied.name: guest_list.xlsx export
assets_supplied.kind: The family's spreadsheet of people expected at the service, with columns for name, household, relationship line and which side of the family they belong to.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Who is coming, and one line about how they knew him. My sister wrote the lines."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The list runs longer than the number of cards actually needed because several couples appear as two rows sharing one household and one line, and a handful of relationship lines run to a full sentence while most are two words. There is no photograph column at all, so binding a plate per family branch requires a column the family never made, built to the merge's own image column contract with filenames the agent controls.

assets_supplied.name: eulogy.txt and transcriptions.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The granddaughter's eulogy as plain prose with emphasis marked, and the family's own typed transcription of every handwritten postcard reverse.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What my daughter will read, and what the backs of the postcards say. We typed them out because you will not be able to read his hand."

acceptance_bar: The framed A4 page is rendered at true print resolution at A4 trim, and the plate on it is placed so the subject is whole rather than cropped by the frame's own fitting.

The book comes back as a native editable document the family can change captions in until the day before, with every plate actually visible in it and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own numeric weight.

The plates sit together as one book when turned page by page: one black point, one sense of warmth, one weight of print. A plate that cannot be brought to the set is treated as its own thing deliberately and said so in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.

No delivered file exceeds its source scan's pixel dimensions, and no tool's silent resize goes unreported. The 1200 px scans are placed at a size they can actually hold and the note says where that constrained the layout.

Exactly one keepsake card per household attending, not one per row, with no duplicate card for a couple and none missing. If the count shipped is not the count the list implies, the note says which rows were merged and why.
Every supplied asset is listed in the delivery manifest as used, reference-only, superseded, or rejected with a concrete reason; no input disappears silently.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the 1968 run can join the book at all in colour. The correction that brings the rest of the colour era to the house neutral is applied to those prints and reports success, and each one looks better on its own than it did. What only appears when they are laid beside the corrected 1930s and 1990s plates is that the two worst have not arrived: their dye layers have shifted far enough that the move which neutralises the cast takes the skin toward green, and pushing further does not converge because the hue range available is moderate rather than complementary. There is no readout for how far an emulsion will travel; it is a property of that print, and the evidence is the set, not the file.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the only way to learn how far a shifted print will move is to move it and look at it beside the others, and there is no earlier moment at which the answer exists. Nothing states it: the brief says the 1968 prints have gone strange and pink and asks for a book, while the acceptance line about the plates sitting together is the family's own standard rather than a disclosure. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is an era level treatment decision that changes what the book is, not a re-execution of the same plan.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Lay the corrected colour plates beside the corrected monochrome plates and judge them as a book turns them. For the prints that will not come, stop chasing the neutral and take a deliberate decision instead: carry that era as a monochromatic tint keyed to the book's warmth so it reads as its own chapter rather than as a failure, or place the two worst small and late rather than as full plates. Then re-cut those plates to the sizes the new decision implies, and record the choice in the note so the family is told rather than shown.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A memory book in which the summer of 1968, the only colour record of the man's young family, turns up as two pink faced plates among ninety years of otherwise settled pages, handed round a Congregational hall by people who remember that summer.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cards and the framed page actually carry what they claim. Two things arrive only on the rendered pages. First, the funeral home's relationship line frame is a fixed measure sized for the two and three word entries the 2019 list happened to hold, so the handful of longer lines the sister wrote do not spill and do not error, they simply stop rendering at the frame's last line: the card looks finished, the merge reports success and every file opens. Second, how the merge fits a landscape plate into the framed page's portrait graphic frame, whether it centres and what it clips, appears in no readout at all, so a plate that was cut correctly to its own subject can still arrive with the subject cut by the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it and care does not help, because both failures present as ordinary success in every response and the frame's true text capacity depends on an applied face and size that a retired designer set and that no tool reports. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a card carrying a name and one line, and the acceptance lines about lines in full at trim and a whole subject on the framed page are the family's own standards rather than warnings. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to change what is bound and how, shortening nothing and instead re-cutting plates to the frame's own proportion and taking the long lines back to the sister for her own shorter wording.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Open and read every rendered card at trim against the normalised list, string by string, rather than judging thumbnails. For each line that stops short, do not shorten the sister's words: take them back to the family for their own decision, and meanwhile re-cut every plate destined for the framed page to that graphic frame's own proportion driven by a selection bbox on the subject, re-merge, re-render at print resolution, and read the pages again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Sixty keepsake cards handed to mourners at the door, several of them carrying a sentence about how that person knew Walter Fernwood that stops mid phrase at the paper's edge, beside a framed A4 page on which his head is cropped by the plate frame, discovered at the service.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the importer actually did to the book's plate construct. The obvious way to give a heritage keepsake its feel is to lay each plate as a mounted print: a soft aged paper texture over the ground, a gently softened plate edge, and a two layer shadow that lifts the plate off the page. All of it exports without a single warning. What comes back is not what was authored: the blend that made the paper texture sit in the page is gone and the texture element arrives as an opaque slab, the softened edge arrives hard, and only the first shadow layer survives, so the plate reads as a flat cut out card. None of this is visible in the rendered preview either, because the preview returns the first root only and the plate pages are pages three onward. The returned markup is the only channel through which any of it can be known.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the construct has to be authored and exported before its normalisation exists to be read, and the preview cannot reach the pages where it lives. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a dignified book and never mentions textures, edges or shadows, and the acceptance line about the book reading as one calm is the family's own standard. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to rebuild the plate treatment out of different materials, which pushes work back into the imaging surface rather than re-exporting the same document.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read the returned markup root by root against what was authored, and rebuild everything that did not survive using means that do: carry the paper feel as a tinted ground and as grain applied to the plate itself in the imaging surface before it is inlined, replace the softened edge with a plate that was cut with its own margin, reduce the lift to the single shadow that survives, then re-author, re-run the readiness check and re-export, and reconcile the markup again page by page.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A memory book whose plate pages, from page three to the colophon, carry an opaque grey slab across the photographs where an aged paper texture was intended, delivered to a family five weeks after a death and printed for a service they cannot rerun.

decision_gates: Which deliverables go to the merge surface and which to authored canvases, given that the family wants the printed pieces to match 2019 and the book to stay editable.
Whether damage sits inside the picture or in the margin, and therefore whether a crop is a lawful remedy or a placement decision is the only honest answer.
What to do with the four files that are photographs of framed prints rather than scans, carrying reflection and keystone that no tool here removes.
How far to carry the 1968 run toward the house neutral before the correction stops being a correction, and what the deliberate alternative is if it will not come.
Whether the postcard reverses are treated as pictures or as documents, and how legibility is bought without turning cream card grey.
Which plates the 1200 px scans can carry, and what the book grid gives up because of it.
Which guest list rows collapse onto one card, which is a family convention rather than a data rule, and how to say so rather than deciding silently.
What to do about a relationship line that will not fit, when shortening the sister's words is not the agent's call to make.

Final files open successfully, use unambiguous names, match the stated dimensions and formats, and include editable sources only where the scoped deliverable requires them.

why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and this shoebox into a frontier image model and it returns beautiful restored photographs. IDENTITY: these are Walter Fernwood's actual family, his father's actual hand on the back of an actual postcard, and a regenerated face or a rebuilt torn corner is a fabrication of a dead man's life presented to the people who are burying him. The client says it outright: do not invent anything that is not in the photographs. SPEC: the family needs one A6 keepsake card per household bound to the sister's own words in full at trim, matching a 2019 press file so the two pieces sit together on a shelf, plus an A4 framed page at true print resolution with the subject whole. EDITABILITY: the book is defined by being editable, because captions change until the day before the service and there is no time and no money for a redo. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did this placeholder get created, does this line reach the end of the sister's sentence at trim, did this era actually arrive beside the others, did the page that cannot be previewed survive the import.
